predecessors.name: Asuka Japan
predecessors.text: the whole realm, the capital moving from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō in 710, with the Ideha (Akita) foothold gained in 709 ('In 709, the fort of Ideha was created close to present day Akita')

successors.name: Heian Japan
successors.text: the whole realm, the capital moving to Heian-kyō in 794, with the Akita foothold and the Miyagi frontier forts (Taga 724, Momonofu 758) the Nara court held

ledger.x: 724: Taga Castle founded on the Sendai plain.
794: the war passes to the Heian dossier.
794: the court moves to Heian-kyō; the Nara period ends.

wars.name: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu rebellion
wars.outcome: 'In 740, a member of the Fujiwara clan, Hirotsugu, launched a rebellion from his base in Fukuoka, Kyushu'; the page gives no outcome sentence; no border moved.

wars.name: Fujiwara no Nakamaro rebellion
wars.outcome: 'Nakamaro rose up in arms in 764 but was quickly crushed.'

wars.name: Thirty-Eight Years' War
wars.outcome: The Nara court held the Sendai plain and lost Monou (774); the war continued under the Heian court until 'Aterui's surrender in 802' and the end in 811 (Heian dossier).

certainty.note: The northern frontier is a line of stockades on the Sendai plain and the Japan Sea coast ('the territory between Akita and the northwest was not under government control'); the Hayato south and the islands are not on the pages opened.
